questions.question: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly to describe an action that has no specific time mentioned?
options: I have lived here since 2010.
I have lived here for five years.
I lived here for five years.
I have lived here in 2010.
questions.answer: I have lived here for five years.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative form of the adjective 'good'.
options: more good
gooder
better
most good

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the second conditional to talk about an imaginary situation?
options: If I have money, I will buy a car.
If I had money, I would buy a car.
If I have money, I would buy a car.
If I had money, I will buy a car.
questions.answer: If I had money, I would buy a car.

questions.question: Select the sentence that correctly uses a modal verb to give advice.
options: You should eat more vegetables.
You must eat more vegetables.
You can eat more vegetables.
You ought to eat more vegetables.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the gerund after the preposition 'avoid'?
options: He avoids to smoke.
He avoids smoking.
He avoids smoke.
He avoids from smoking.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the correct linker: '______ it was raining, we decided to go for a walk.'
options: Because
Although
So
But

questions.question: Which sentence uses the past continuous correctly to describe an action in progress at a specific time in the past?
options: I was sleeping when the phone rang.
I sleep when the phone rang.
I slept when the phone rang.
I had slept when the phone rang.
questions.answer: I was sleeping when the phone rang.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the infinitive after the verb 'want'.
options: I want go to the cinema.
I want to go to the cinema.
I want going to the cinema.
I want went to the cinema.
questions.answer: I want to go to the cinema.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the superlative form of 'happy'?
options: She is more happy than me.
She is happier than me.
She is the most happy.
She is happiest.

questions.question: Select the sentence that correctly uses the third conditional to describe a past possibility that did not happen.
options: If I studied harder, I would pass the exam.
If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I had studied harder, I will have passed the exam.
questions.answer: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
